prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: parking lot collision in Pearland, Texas. Injury: back strain. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1037; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record. I'm the plaintiff in this matter, so you already have it in the filings.

Q: Fair enough. Let's go over the accident. Where were you when it happened?

A: I was in a parking lot at a shopping center in Pearland, Texas. I had just pulled into a space near the grocery store entrance.

Q: What were you doing right before the impact?

A: I was backing out of the space to leave. I checked my mirror and I saw nothing coming, so I started reversing slowly.

Q: What happened next?

A: A pickup truck came down the aisle, faster than you'd expect for a parking lot. It hit the rear passenger side of my car. The impact spun my car partly around and pushed me back against the seat.

Q: Did you get out of the vehicle?

A: Yes, once I could get my door open. The other driver was already out, and we talked for a few minutes while people walked past.

Q: When did you first notice pain?

A: Not right away. I felt fine at the scene, just shaken. By that evening my lower back was tight, and by the next morning it was a sharp ache that got worse when I bent over or sat too long.

Q: Who treated you after the accident?

A: I went to an urgent care clinic the following day. They took X-rays, prescribed muscle relaxers and an anti-inflammatory, and told me to rest and see a physical therapist.

Q: Have you been going to physical therapy?

A: Yes, I've been going about twice a week. The exercises help some days more than others. My therapist has me working on core strength and stretching.

Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?

A: It's affected a lot. I used to coach my nephew's soccer team on weekends, and I've had to hand that off to my brother. Driving longer than twenty or thirty minutes is uncomfortable, and I can't lift our grocery bags without my back catching.

Q: Have you missed any work?

A: I missed about a week in the first few days after the accident. Since then I've been working at my desk, but I stand up often and I can't sit through long meetings the way I used to.

Q: Do you have any prior problems with your lower back?

A: I had a minor strain years ago from moving furniture, but it resolved with a few weeks of rest. Before this accident I had no ongoing treatment.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything you'd like to add?

A: Only that I want to get back to normal. I'm hopeful the therapy continues to help.
